narrative:
The model estimated a 97% probability that you would fail the bar exam on your first attempt. Because the law school uses predicted bar success in admission decisions, that very high risk estimate is why your application was rejected.

The strongest factor was your third-year class-standing decile: at 1, it is far below the average accepted student’s 5.79, and it pushed the prediction strongly toward failure. The next most influential factor was your LSAT score of 25, well below the accepted-student average of 37.18; this also pushed toward failure. The third factor was your first-year decile of 1, compared with an accepted-student average of 6.00, which further increased the predicted risk. Your undergraduate GPA of 3.60 was above the accepted average, but it was not enough to offset those concerns. Your gender and race were not used.

To improve a future application, focus on the areas that most affected this prediction: plan to retake the LSAT with preparation, meet an admissions adviser to discuss how your class standing is evaluated, and consider delaying application until you can show stronger academic or test evidence. Ask whether supplemental explanations or a later application cycle would let the committee review your progress more fully.
